items.text: An ambitious Australian law, which came into effect last December to protect youth mental health, bans children under 16 from having social media accounts. However, half a year later, studies show the ban is largely ineffective. Most underage users can easily access and create new accounts on platforms like Snapchat, Instagram, and YouTube. Although the government recommends strict verification steps, tech companies mostly rely on simple self-declarations of age that children can easily bypass. Sometimes, children ask their parents to complete face verification for them, or they continue using their old, unverified accounts. Furthermore, software designed to estimate a user’s age based on online activity rarely works. In response to this non-compliance , the Australian government has doubled the maximum fines for tech giants and warned them of potential court action. Despite these early struggles, countries around the world, including the EU, are closely watching Australia’s progress as they consider implementing similar bans. Difficult words: verification (proving that something is true, correct, or real), self-declaration (telling or writing something about yourself without showing any official papers to prove it), non-compliance (a failure or refusal to follow an official rule, law, or agreement). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In December, Australia started a new law that stops children under 16 from using social media. The government wanted to protect the mental health of young people. But six months later, the law is not working well. Studies show that most kids can still easily open and use accounts on Snapchat, Instagram, and YouTube. The tech companies don’t check the age of their users carefully. Children can lie about their age, or they can ask their parents to help them pass the face checks . The special computer programs which try to guess a user’s age don’t work well either. Now, the government is very angry with the big tech companies. They doubled the fines for companies which don’t follow the rules. Other countries in the world are watching Australia to see if they should make similar laws. Difficult words: mental health (how you feel in your mind, how happy you are, and how well you cope with everyday life and stress), face check (using a camera or special computer software to look at a person’s face to check who they are or how old they look), fine (money you must pay when you break a rule or law). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Australia has a new law since December. This law says that children under 16 cannot use social media like YouTube or Instagram. The government wants to help kids feel better. But the law is not working. Many children still use these apps every day. It is very easy to make a new account. Children can just write a false age , or their parents can help them. The big computer companies do not stop the children. Now, the government is angry. They want these companies to pay a lot of money if they do not follow the rules. Other countries are looking at Australia to see what happens next. Difficult words: law (an official rule), government (the people who control a country), age (how old you are). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The technology used in swimming is very advanced, and swimsuits are a key piece of equipment. Designers constantly work on improving swimsuits, and although they might look similar, at the elite level, they are highly engineered and costly. New suit technology often appears at the Olympics, aiming to enhance performance. The sports governing body regulates the materials and design; however, companies still push the limits to create the best suits. Athletes try out different suits to find the best fit. For example, the latest Arena suit includes a new material with compression and flexibility. It takes only two minutes instead of the usual ten to try it on, and athletes feel more buoyant in the water. Testing suits in water with cameras show how they minimize bubbles and help streamline the body. Ultimately, you’ll need to test a few times before deciding on the best suit for race day. Difficult words: elite (the best-trained, best-educated, or richest group in society), engineered (designed and built using scientific principles), buoyant (able to float). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The technology in swimming is very advanced , especially in swimsuits. Designers always try to improve them, making them better for swimmers. The Olympic swimsuits are very expensive and high-tech . The sports body has rules about what materials and designs athletes can use, but companies still try to make the best suits. Athletes test different suits to find the best one. For example, the new Arena suit is easy to put on. It takes only two minutes instead of the usual ten. It makes swimmers feel light in the water. Testing in water shows that the suit helps reduce bubbles and helps athletes swim faster. But you must test a few more times before choosing your suit for the race. Difficult words: advanced (modern and well-developed), designer (a person who creates new things), high-tech (using the most modern methods, designs, machines, and so on). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Swimsuits are very important for swimming. Designers make them better and better. Now, before the Olympics, athletes are looking for the best swimsuits. Olympic swimsuits are very expensive. The sports body makes rules for what materials and designs companies can use. But companies still try to make the best suits. They use new materials. Swimmers test different suits to find the best one. The new Arena suit is easy to put on. You only need two minutes for that. Normally, you would need ten minutes. The suit also makes you feel light in the water. It reduces bubbles, which makes you swim faster. Difficult words: designer (a person who creates new things), body (a group of people who work together and decide on something), reduce (to make smaller or less in amount or size). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The legendary Welsh singer Bonnie Tyler has unexpectedly passed away at the age of 75 in a hospital in Portugal, following an illness she had been treated for since May. Her family and team shared their deep heartbreak over her sudden death, which has shocked fans worldwide because recent updates suggested she was recovering well after emergency surgery. Best known for her powerful, timeless ballads like Total Eclipse of the Heart and Holding Out for a Hero , Tyler possessed a unique, raspy voice that made her instantly recognizable . Interestingly, her famous gravelly vocals were the accidental result of screaming in frustration too soon after a throat operation in the 1970s. Her music connected with generations of listeners, and recently passed over a billion streams on Spotify and trended on modern platforms like TikTok. Tributes have poured in from officials and music lovers, who celebrated her incredible vocal range, emotional depth, and lasting musical legacy. Difficult words: raspy (sounding rough and harsh, like when you have a cold or a sore throat), recognizable (easy to know or identify because you have seen or heard it before), gravelly (a voice that sounds rough, low, and a bit dry, like tiny stones are rubbing together in the throat). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The famous Welsh singer Bonnie Tyler died at the age of 75. Her family announced that she passed away in a hospital in Portugal after being sick for some time. This news shocked many people because everyone thought she was getting better after surgery. Bonnie Tyler was loved for her big hit songs like Total Eclipse of the Heart and Holding Out for a Hero . She had a very special voice that people could recognize immediately. She got this unique voice by accident after a throat operation in the 1970s. People of all ages still love her music, and her songs have millions of plays online today. Many fans and friends are very sad about her death, and they will always remember her beautiful and powerful singing. Difficult words: pass away (to die), recognize (to know who someone is or what something is), u nique (very special and different from everything else). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Bonnie Tyler is a very famous singer. She is from Wales. She dies. She is 75 years old. She is in a hospital in Portugal because she is sick. Her family and fans are very sad today. Bonnie is famous for her great songs like Total Eclipse of the Heart . Everyone knows Bonnie because she has a very special, deep voice . She loves to sing for young and old people, and she is very kind to her fans. Today, millions of people still listen to her music on their computers and phones. She is a great star. People will never forget her beautiful songs. Difficult words: fan (a person who loves a singer, band, or sports team), voice (the sound that comes out of your mouth when you speak, sing, or make a noise), forget (to not remember something from the past). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A groundbreaking experiment involving cancer cells sent to space has revealed startling insights into cancer behavior. Scientists observed that cancer cells multiplied rapidly in space, tripling in size within just 10 days compared to the 10-year timeframe required on Earth. This unhinged growth is attributed to microgravity, which alters cellular behavior. Researchers focused on the adar1 gene, known for its role in cancer recurrence and resistance to therapy. By genetically manipulating this gene, scientists successfully inhibited cancer cell cloning, suggesting a potential ‘kill switch’ for cancer. A drug called Rebecsinib showed promise in targeting the adar1 gene. Furthermore, astronauts played a vital role in the study, contributing their blood for stem cell analysis. Although these findings offer hope for cancer treatment, the drug is not yet ready for human use. However, researchers aim to begin clinical trials soon to bring this innovative approach to cancer therapy. Difficult words: unhinge (to throw into disorder), recurrence (the reappearance of a medical condition after its apparent disappearance), inhibit (to prevent an action or process). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

An experiment which sent cancer cells to space brought important findings about cancer growth and possible treatments . In space, cancer cells grow much faster than on Earth, and it happens thanks to microgravity . Scientists focused on the adar1 gene, which plays a role in cancer recurrence . Scientists manipulated this gene, they were able to stop cancer cell cloning. The drug called Rebecsinib showed good results in targeting the adar1 gene. Astronauts provided their blood for some experiments. These findings bring hope for cancer patients, but the drug is not yet ready for human use. Researchers want to begin clinical trials soon. Difficult words: treatment (medical care for an illness or injury), microgravity (very weak gravity, as in space), recurrence (when an illness appears again). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists study how cancer cells grow in space. The result surprises everyone. Cancer cells grow much faster than on Earth. Scientists believe that the reason is weak gravity . Scientists focus on a gene called adar1. This gene makes cancer return. When scientists change this gene, they stop cancer cells from multiplying . A drug named Rebecsinib works against this gene. Astronauts help by giving their blood for testing. However, the drug is not ready for people yet. Scientists hope to start tests soon to use this new way to stop cancer. Difficult words: cell (the smallest part of a living thing), gravity (the force which pulls things towards the Earth), multiply (to increase a lot in number). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A four-year study tracking over 1,200 men in Utah has revealed that breathing in common air pollutants like ozone and nitrogen dioxide can negatively affect their reproductive health. The research shows that exposure to these man-made contaminants during sperm development is linked to subtle DNA changes. Specifically, it affects a process called methylation, which acts like a switch turning genes on and off. Experts warn that these changes can lead to decreased sperm counts and lower motility, which is the sperm’s ability to swim. Because these pollutants come from heavy industrial activity and busy city traffic fumes, men living in larger, highly polluted cities face a greater risk of fertility issues. These genetic changes inside the testes can have long-term consequences not only for the individual’s fertility but also for their future children. To protect themselves, people are advised to reduce unnecessary exposure by wearing face masks during heavy smog or taking occasional trips out of the city. Difficult words: exposure (a situation where you are not protected from something dangerous or dirty, allowing it to affect your body), contaminant (a substance that makes something like air, water, or food dirty, unsafe, or impure), consequence (a result or effect of an action or situation, which is often bad or unpleasant). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A new four-year study shows that dirty air can hurt male fertility . Scientists studied more than 1,200 men and found that breathing in common city pollution causes small changes in sperm DNA. These changes affect genes and can make it harder for men to have children. The biggest problems come from ozone and nitrogen dioxide, which are dangerous gases from cars and factories. Because of this, men who live in big, busy cities often have a lower sperm count, and their sperm cannot swim well. This is a serious problem because these changes can also affect the health of future babies. Experts say it is difficult for everyone to leave the city, but men can protect themselves. They can lead a healthy lifestyle, wear face masks when there is a lot of smog , and visit nature outside the city. Difficult words: fertility (the ability of a person to produce babies), pollution (dangerous, dirty, or poisonous substances in the air, water, or land), smog (smoke, gases, and chemicals which form a thick, dark fog over busy cities). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Dirty air from cars and factories can be bad for men. A new study looks at 1,200 men over four years. Scientists find that bad air changes sperm . These changes can stop men from having babies. Men who live in big, busy cities breathe in bad smoke every day. This smoke makes their bodies weaker. Their sperm is not so good. This is a big problem for their future children, too. It is not easy to move away from big cities. But men can wear face masks when the air is very dirty . It also helps to eat good food and walk in the forest sometimes. Difficult words: sperm (a small part in a man’s body which can make a woman pregnant), breathe in (to take air into your lungs through your nose or mouth), dirty (not clean). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

For almost 2,000 years, ancient scrolls found in Herculaneum remained unreadable due to fire and volcanic ash from Mount Vesuvius’ eruption in 79 AD. Italian scientists are now employing artificial intelligence and advanced infrared imaging to piece together the lost text. These techniques have revealed new insights into the final days of the Greek philosopher Plato, including details about his burial and activities before his death at 81. Professor Graziano Ranocchia from the University of Pisa leads the team behind this breakthrough . It not only uncovers Plato’s burial site near the Academy but also promises to help decode other unread scrolls. Difficult words: scroll (a roll of paper for writing on), breakthrough (a sudden and important discovery or development), decode (to figure out or understand). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Volcanic ash from the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD covered the Herculaneum scrolls . Now, thanks to advanced technology, Italian scientists finally revealed their secrets. Through artificial intelligence and infrared imaging, scientists decoded details about the Greek philosopher Plato. Plato died at the age of 81, and the scrolls tell us about his last days and his burial, too. Professor Graziano Ranocchiea from the University of Pisa leads the team. This discovery tells us about Plato’s burial site near the Academy and promises to help decode other unread scrolls. Difficult words: scroll (a roll of paper for writing on), advanced (modern), decode (to figure out or understand), burial site (an area where dead bodies are in the ground). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 79 AD Mount Vesuvius erupts. The ash covers the Herculaneum scrolls . Now, scientists find the scrolls. They are using smart technology to read them. They find out about Plato. Plato is a famous philosopher. He dies when he is 81 years old. The scrolls tell us about his life. Now, we also know more about where his body is. Professor Graziano Ranocchia from an Italian university leads the team. They want to use the same technology to read other scrolls, too. Finding the scrolls is very important. It tells us a lot about Plato and history . Difficult words: ash (the grey powder which we get when something burns), scroll (a roll of paper for writing on), history (things which happen in the past). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Social media platforms are being flooded with ultra-realistic ads created by AI to sell products that either don’t exist or turn out to be cheap junk . Scammers use AI because it allows them to generate professional-looking videos and fake customer testimonials quickly and cheaply without real photoshoots. These ads appear on both shady websites and legitimate platforms like Amazon. Clicking these dangerous links can instantly download malware onto a user’s machine or expose them to phishing attacks, which can lead to repeated unauthorized credit card transactions and data theft. Experts note that these ads easily slip through automated moderation systems due to the sheer volume of new content. To stay safe, users should always do a reverse image search, carefully verify unfamiliar website URLs, look out for strange bot-like comments, and remain deeply cautious of suspicious celebrity endorsements or any online offers that look too perfect to be true. Difficult words: ultra-realistic (looking or sounding so incredibly real that it is almost impossible to see that it was made by a computer), junk (things that have no real value, are broken, or are of very bad quality; trash), customer testimonials (short statements, reviews, or videos where people say how good a product is and why they love buying it), sheer (very large size, huge amount, or great number of something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Scammers are now using AI to make very realistic fake ads on social media. They show beautiful pictures of things like coffee mugs or toys, but these products are not real. When people click the links to buy them, they can end up on dangerous websites. These websites can secretly steal private credit card information or install bad programs on computers. Scammers make money quickly and then disappear . These fake ads are even on big websites like Amazon because computers cannot catch them all. To protect yourself, you should never trust prices that are too low. You can check the pictures on the internet first, look at the website address carefully, and read the comments to see if they look real. Difficult words: realistic (when something looks real and natural), ad (a short video, picture, or text to show a product and make people want to buy it), disappear (to suddenly go away). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There are many new fake ads on social media today. Scammers use AI to make beautiful videos of things which do not exist. When you click the link to buy a toy or a cup, you can lose your money. Sometimes, these bad websites take your credit card numbers or break your computer. It is very easy and cheap for scammers to make these ads. They can put them on big web shops too, for example, Amazon. If a price is too low, it is usually a trick . You must be careful. Always check the name of the website before you give it your money. Difficult words: fake (not real), ad (a short video, picture, or text to show a product and make people want to buy it), scammer (a person who uses fake websites or other tricks to také your money or data), trick (something dishones what a person does to steal something from you). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Danish toymaker Lego has abandoned a high-profile project to replace oil-based plastics in its bricks. They discovered that using a new material made from recycled polyethylene terephthalate (RPET) would result in higher carbon emissions. Lego’s CEO Niels Christiansen explained that they had tested numerous materials but failed to find a suitable alternative. Nevertheless, Lego remains committed to sustainability and plans to create toys from eco-friendly materials by 2032. The company embarked on this journey in 2020 to replace its plastic bricks with sustainable options. The main challenge was finding a material that was both environmentally friendly and retained the same color, shine, and sound as the oil-based plastic bricks. Difficult words: abandon (to give up), embark (to start a journey), retain (continue to have, keep). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Lego, a famous toy company from Denmark, stopped trying to make its bricks without using oil-based plastics. Lego found out that a new material which they tried actually produces more carbon emissions. Lego’s CEO said that they tested many materials but couldn’t find a good one but they are still working on this and want to make their toys using eco-friendly materials by 2032. Lego started trying to replace plastic bricks with eco-friendly ones in 2020. The hard part is finding a material that is good for the environment and still looks and sounds like the old plastic bricks. Difficult words: oil-based (using oil or materials which come from oil), eco-friendly (not harming the natural world), replace (to use something instead of something else). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Lego is a famous Danish toy company. They try to make their bricks without using oil-based plastics. But it does not work well. They have to stop. The new material makes more emissions than the material which they use normally. The boss of Lego says that they cannot find a good enough material. But the company still wants to use good materials by 2032. Lego starts trying this in 2020. It is hard because they need a material which does not harm the natural world. But at the same time, the material must look and sound like the old bricks. Difficult words: brick (a small block for building houses), oil-based (using oil or materials which come from oil), emission (a small thing which gets in the air and makes it dirty). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists are questioning whether FIFA’s current hydration breaks are sufficient to protect football players competing in extreme heat and humidity. Researchers tested FIFA’s official policy by measuring how a three-minute break in each half affects trained male and female athletes at a high temperature of 32 degrees. The study revealed that these breaks are valuable only if they include active cooling measures. This means players must drink very cold liquids and place ice-water-soaked towels or cooling braces around their necks. The experiments proved that active cooling leads to significant reductions in both thermal and cardiovascular strain , and helps lower the body’s core temperature and heart rate. The next scientific step is to study the energy production of elite footballers and their clothing under different weather conditions. This will help find the exact safety threshold where extreme heat becomes dangerous for athletes. Difficult words: hydration (drinking enough water or healthy liquids so that your body has what it needs to work properly), strain (physical pressure, stress, or extreme tiredness on your body or heart), elite (the absolute best, highest, or most talented group of people in a field), threshold (a specific level, point, or limit at which something completely changes or becomes dangerous). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Scientists are checking if short water breaks during football matches really protect players in extreme heat. Researchers tested the official rules during hot weather. They looked at what happens to the bodies of male and female players during a three-minute break in each half of the game. They found that these breaks only help if players use active cooling. This means that players must drink very cold drinks and put wet, icy towels around their necks. The test showed that this special cooling quickly lowers the body temperature and helps the heart rate go down. It also makes the athletes feel much better. The next step for scientists is to study players’ clothes and how much they run. This will help them find a safe limit for playing sports in hot weather. Difficult words: extreme (very great or more dangerous than what is normal or usual), towel (a piece of soft cloth that you use for drying your body after a shower), limit (the furthest point or highest amount which is allowed, safe, or possible). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Is drinking water during a football game enough when the weather is very hot? Scientists do a test with professional players. They give players a short three-minute break in the game. The test shows that players need more than just water. They need active cooling. This means that they must drink very cold water and put cold towels on their necks. This helps the body stay cool, and the heart beat normally. It also makes the players feel good. Now, scientists want to do more tests with football clothes. They want to find a safe rule so that players do not get sick in the hot sun. Difficult words: professional (when you do a sport as a job, not for fun), towel (a piece of soft cloth that you use for drying your body after a shower), rule (an official statement of what you must or must not do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In today’s digital era where screens and keyboards dominate , we often underestimate the importance of handwriting. Experts say that handwriting plays a key role in cognitive development, memory retention , and academic performance. Why should children continue to practice writing? A study published in the National Library of Medicine discovered that handwriting contributes to functional brain development. Writing letters and words is particularly beneficial for young children’s brains compared to other forms of sensorimotor practice. Moreover, legible handwriting can lead to better grades, regardless of the content. According to Krista Griffin, a professor of elementary education, writing helps in the connection between letters and sounds for children. Therefore, opting for pencil and paper over typing on a phone could be advantageous. Difficult words: dominate (to be the most important person or thing), cognitive (related to thinking and reasoning), retention (the ability to keep or continue having something), sensorimotor (relating to both the sensory and motor functions of an organism). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

These days, screens and keyboards are becoming more important than handwriting. But experts say that handwriting is very important for our memory, thinking, and also academic success. The question is whether children should continue to practice writing. Some studies suggest that handwriting helps develop our brains, especially for young children. Moreover, if you write well, it can lead to better grades at school. Writing helps children connect letters with sounds, which is healthy for the brain. Research suggests that physically writing something down improves working memory, which is something typing on a keyboard cannot do. Therefore, using pencil and paper may be more beneficial than typing on a phone. Difficult words: academic (related to school and learning), keyboard (a panel of keys on a computer or phone), beneficial (helpful, useful). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Today’s world is full of technology. We look at screens a lot. We do not write in hand so much anymore. Handwriting seems less important. But is it? Experts say that writing in hand is very important, especially for children. Handwriting helps the brain develop well. Neat handwriting can even help children get better grades in school. Writing helps children connect letters with sounds. It is different from typing on a computer. Writing with a pencil and paper may be better for memory. It helps improve thinking. So, handwriting is still important for children to learn and practice. Difficult words: develop (to grow or change), neat (clean or smooth), improve (to make something better). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Prince Harry and six other high-profile people, including Sir Elton John and Elizabeth Hurley, have lost their High Court privacy case against Associated Newspapers Limited, the publisher of the Daily Mail. The claimants sued the publisher for a serious breach of privacy. Allegedly, reporters used unlawful methods like phone tapping and deception to get information for articles for over twenty years. However, the judge dismissed the cases because the claimants failed to provide enough evidence to prove their claims. The judge also said that personal suspicion is not sufficient in court. While the publisher celebrated the verdict, the case represents a massive financial loss for both sides. Meanwhile, Harry is in London for charity events amid fresh communication problems with the royal family. The palace rejected his request to stay at Buckingham Palace due to a missed deadline, and his family remained in the US because of ongoing disagreements over police protection. Difficult words: high-profile (very famous and important), claimant (a person who starts a legal process in a court of law to get justice, money, or a right), phone-taping (secretly listening to or recording someone else’s private telephone calls). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Prince Harry and six other famous people, including Elton John, lost a big court case against the publisher of the Daily Mail newspaper. They said that reporters broke privacy laws by secretly listening to their phone calls and taking personal information for more than twenty years. The newspaper company always said this was not true. Today, the judge dropped the case because the famous group didn’t have enough real evidence to prove their stories. The judge said that simply thinking something happened is not enough for a court. This loss is very expensive for both sides. At the same time, Harry is visiting London alone. He wanted to stay at the royal palace, but the royal family said no because he didn’t ask in time. His wife and children stayed at home in the US. Difficult words: privacy (your right to keep your personal life, feelings, and secret stories away from other people and the media), evidence (facts, objects, or information that show clearly that something is true or really happened), prove (to show that something is true). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Prince Harry and six other famous people lose a big fight in a London court. They go to court against a big newspaper company. Harry says that the journalists do bad things to get his secret information and stories. For example, they listen to the phone calls. But the judge says today that Harry and his friends do not have real facts to prove the story. The judge says that feeling bad is not enough for a court. It is a very long and expensive fight. Now Harry is in London alone for his work. He is not staying with the King because there are many problems between them. Difficult words: secret (something what people do not know about), prove (to show that something is true), expensive (when something costs a lot of money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Doctors in Belgium are witnessing a rise in patients with severe nose issues due to increased cocaine usage. These patients are typically in their forties and with privileged socio-economic backgrounds, and they often suffer from nasal obstructions and damage to the mucous membrane and cartilage . Cocaine narrows blood vessels in the nose which leads to tissue damage and perforations. When the perforation is wider, it leads to a collapse of the nasal pyramid, which is visible from the outside. Reconstruction of the nose may be necessary for severe cases. Despite a surge in cocaine use in Belgium over the past five years, the number of operations remains limited. The reason is that many patients struggle to undergo surgery due to the need to abstain from cocaine for at least six months for proper healing. Difficult words: mucous membrane (the thin soft tissue that covers the inside of the nose, mouth, and so on), cartilage (the strong tissue in the joints and other places such as the nose, throat, and ears), abstain (to choose not to do or have something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Doctors in Belgium are treating more patients with nose problems. These patients are usually in their forties, they are managers, teachers, or people who work in banking. And they use cocaine. Cocaine narrows blood vessels in the nose, which damages the tissue and makes holes. In some cases, patients need a nose reconstruction . But many patients can’t undergo surgery because they mustn’t use cocaine for at least six months before the surgery for good healing. So although there are more cocaine users, the number of surgeries is not growing much. Difficult words: vessel (a tube which carries blood through the body), tissue (the material which animals and plants are made of), reconstruction (rebuilding or repairing something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Doctors in Belgium are helping more people with nose problems. These people use cocaine . These people are often between 40 and 50 years old. They are managers, teachers, or bankers. Cocaine narrows blood vessels in the nose. This hurts the nose. There can be holes. Some people may need surgery to fix their noses. But they must stop using cocaine for six months before the surgery. That is why not many people can have surgery. It is hard for them to stop using cocaine. Difficult words: cocaine (a drug from a dry coca plant), narrow (to make or become less wide), vessel (a tube through which blood travels in the body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Paris Court of Appeal has agreed with the decision that far-right leader Marine Le Pen is guilty of misusing EU funds, but it reduced her punishment. Her original five-year ban from public office was shortened, which means she can legally run in the April 2027 French presidential election. However, the judge also decided she must stay under house arrest for one year and wear an electronic ankle tag . This creates a major political problem – Le Pen has repeatedly stated she will refuse to run if she is forced to wear a tag, and she claims she wouldn’t feel free to campaign or meet voters normally. Political experts suggest that if Le Pen decides to step down because of this situation, her young partner, Jordan Bardella, will likely take her place as the party’s presidential candidate and launch a completely new political strategy for the election. Difficult words: misuse (to use something in a wrong, bad, or illegal way, especially money or power) , house arrest (a legal punishment where a person is not allowed to leave their home, instead of going to a real prison), tag (a small electronic object attached to a person’s body so that the police know exactly where they are). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A French court decided that political leader Marine Le Pen is guilty of taking public money, but the court changed her punishment . Her old five-year ban from politics is now over, so she can legally run in the next presidential election in April 2027. But there is still a big problem. The judge said Le Pen has to stay at home for one year and wear an electronic tag on her leg. Le Pen said before that she would not run for president if she had to wear this tag because she cannot travel and talk to people normally. Now, Le Pen’s political party must hold a special meeting. If she decides to step down , her young partner Jordan Bardella will probably become the new candidate for the election. Difficult words: guilty (when somebody does something wrong or illegal; or is responsible for a crime), punishment (a bad or difficult thing that someone must experience because they broke a rule or a law), tag (a small electronic object attached to a person’s body so that the police know exactly where they are), step down (to officially leave an important job, position, or political role). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A court in Paris says that Marine Le Pen is guilty. She takes money from the EU. But the court changes her punishment . Now, she can legally run in the election for president in April 2027. But she has a new problem. She must stay at home for one year and wear a special electronic device on her leg. Le Pen says that she hates this device. She will not run if she must wear it. She wants to meet with people face-to-face. If she stops, a young man from her party, Jordan Bardella, will try to become the new president of France. Difficult words: punishment (a bad or difficult thing which someone must experience because they broke a rule or a law), election (a time when people vote to choose a new political leader, president, or government), device (a small machine, tool, or object which does a special job). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Volkswagen is planning to cut tens of thousands of jobs and potentially close European factories because its traditional business model is no longer working. CEO Oliver Blume emphasizes that building cars in Germany for global export has become inefficient due to a declining Chinese market, high regulatory burdens , and competition from aggressive Chinese manufacturers. VW’s previous efficiency plans from 2024 are no longer sufficient to protect its market share. Meanwhile, Chinese carmakers have captured a record 10% of the European market. They successfully bypassed the EU’s 2024 tariffs on fully electric vehicles by shifting their focus to hybrid models. To protect domestic automakers, European politicians are currently discussing the Industrial Accelerator Act. This legislation could introduce new tariffs on hybrids or enforce Made in Europe requirements, which would compel foreign companies to manufacture their vehicles locally within Europe. This trend is already seen in recent partnership deals in Spain. Difficult words: burden (something difficult, heavy, or worrying that you are responsible for or must deal with, like a lot of tax or too many rules), bypass (to avoid), compel (to force a person or a company to do something because of a strong law, a rule, or a difficult situation). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Volkswagen, Europe’s biggest carmaker, wants to cut tens of thousands of jobs and may close some factories. The company’s CEO, Oliver Blume, says their old business model of making cars in Germany for global export doesn’t work anymore. Volkswagen is losing customers in China, and European buyers are spending less money. At the same time, Chinese car companies are growing fast and now hold over 10% of the European market. To avoid high European import taxes on electric cars, Chinese companies started selling more hybrid cars instead. To protect European companies, the EU is now planning new laws. These rules might put taxes on hybrid cars or make foreign companies to build their vehicles inside Europe. Difficult words: business model (a company’s organized plan for how it will make cars or products, sell them, and earn a profit), avoid (to find a clever way around a problem, a rule, or a tax so that you do not have to deal with it or pay it), hybrid car (a modern car that uses two different sources of power: a standard petrol engine and an electric motor). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Volkswagen is a very big car company in Europe. But it has large problems. The boss of the company wants to close factories and cut thousands of jobs. Making cars in Germany is now too expensive. Volkswagen is losing money in China. At the same time, Chinese car companies are selling many new cars in Europe. They now have 10% of the European market . They sell popular hybrid cars . European leaders want to help their car companies. They are talking about new rules. They want taxes on Chinese hybrid cars. The plan is to make these companies build cars inside Europe. Difficult words: cut (to reduce), market (a specific country, area, or group of people where a company can buy and sell its products), hybrid car (a modern car with a petrol engine and an electric motor). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Recycling advocacy group Metal Focus reports that households are accumulating more unused electronics and broken devices. People now store an average of 30 items, up from 20 in four years. Metal Focus identifies top items like remote controls, mobile phones, and hairdryers. Many of us hold onto old gadgets, cables, and remotes, which contributes to this issue. Spring cleaning offers a chance to responsibly declutter ; however, electronic waste is increasing much faster than recycling efforts. Proper disposal matters because electronics contain valuable materials. Material Focus suggests options like sharing or repairing to extend products’ life. Manufacturers could also design more durable and repairable products. The UN warns that global electronic waste is outpacing recycling, and emphasizes the need to save valuable resources. Difficult words: accumulate (to collect a large number of things over a long period), declutter (to remove unnecessary things), outpace (to go or rise faster than). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People keep more unused electronics than they did four years ago, a report says. People kept about 20 items four years ago, but now it is about 30 items. The most popular items are remote controls , phones, and hairdryers. The UN says that there is more electronic waste than companies can recycle. The amount of electronic waste is growing too fast. We are all responsible for this problem, although we want to recycle electronic waste. It is important to get rid of electronic waste properly because there are valuable materials in it. Using these materials again saves resources. Also, sharing or repairing would make things last longer. The problem is that companies often make products which last only a few years and it is not possible to repair them. Difficult words: remote control (a device which we use to control our TV), waste (things and materials which people throw away because they no longer need them), valuable (very important or helpful). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A report says that people keep more unused electronics. Four years ago, one family usually has 20 things. Now, it is about 30. Most people keep remote controls , old phones, and hairdryers. People want to recycle these things. But it is not so easy. There are too many things. Companies are not able to recycle them all. It is not good. These things have important materials in them. We can use these materials again. It saves natural resources . Another problem is that companies do not make good products. Some products do not last long. Also, it is not possible to repair them. People throw them away and buy new things. It is good for companies but not for the natural world. Difficult words: unused (something what we do not use anymore), remote control (a device which we use to control the TV), natural resource s (things such as minerals, wood, coal, gas, and so on). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The EU has introduced a new 3-euro fee on low-value e-commerce parcels from China, which targets major online retailers like Shein, Temu, and AliExpress. Previously, these platforms entered the EU bloc duty-free under a long-standing exemption for goods under 150 euros. However, policymakers and European retailers complained about unfair competition after the number of exempt parcels surged from 1.4 billion to 5.8 billion in 2025. Lawmakers argue that this tax loophole was abused on an industrial scale, which gave Chinese giants a massive competitive advantage over local businesses. Under the new rules, fees are applied per item category in a shipment; for example, a package with three different types of products will incur a 9-euro charge. This decision follows similar strict actions by the US, which completely ended its own low-value import exemptions earlier this year to protect its domestic market. Difficult words: retailer (a person, shop, or online business that sells goods directly to customers for their personal use), exemption (a special permission that says a person or a company doesn’t have to pay a tax or follow a rule), loophole (a small mistake or missing part in a law that allows people to avoid paying taxes or following a rule legally), competitive advantage (a special strength, lower price, or condition that makes one company much better and more successful than its rivals). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The EU starts charging a new 3-euro fee on cheap packages from China. This new rule targets popular online shops like Shein, Temu, and AliExpress. Before this change, these companies didn’t pay import taxes on cheap goods , which helped them sell products at very low prices and grow fast. But European businesses complained that this was unfair. The number of small packages that entered Europe grew from 1.4 billion to 5.8 billion in 2025. Politicians say that Chinese companies abused the old rules. Now, buyers must pay 3 euros for each type of item in a box. For example, a parcel with three different types of items will cost 9 euros. The United States also started a similar tax on Chinese goods earlier this year to help US companies. Difficult words: fee (an amount of money that you must pay for a service), target (to choose a specific person, group, or company to focus on, attack, or change with a new rule), goods (things and objects which people buy and sell). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Europe has a new rule for cheap packages from China. People must now pay a 3-euro fee for every item from shops like Shein, Temu, and AliExpress. In the past, these shops do not pay taxes on things from other countries. This helps them sell clothes and toys for very low prices. But this is not fair for European shops. Too many packages come to Europe, 5.8 billion in 2025. The fee is for every different thing in the package. If you buy three different types of things, you pay 9 euros. The US also has this fee on cheap things from China. They say that they must help US companies. Difficult words: package (a thing in a box which comes to your home), fee (money which you must pay for a service), item (one thing or object which is part of a list or a larger group of things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Istanbul Airport now offers therapy dogs to calm anxious travelers before their flights. The program aims to reduce stress and anxiety among passengers. Travelers like Anastasia Podmazova find comfort in petting dogs like Kuki, praising the service. Positive feedback has prompted the airport to consider expanding the project from five to ten dogs. Abdulkadir Demirtas, a customer experience manager, highlights the proven benefits of animal-human interaction in reducing stress. Dog expert Murat Cengiz Koca ensures that the trained dogs remain calm and unreactive to sounds or people, making them suitable for the role. Difficult words: prompt (to cause or encourage something to happen), unreactive (not responding to stimuli or external factors). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Istanbul Airport now has therapy dogs to help travelers relax before flights. Some people are anxious before flying and therapy dogs are a great help. Passengers like Anastasia Podmazova welcome the service, and they find comfort in petting dogs like Kuki. Because of positive feedback, the airport is thinking of having five more dogs. That would make ten dogs altogether. Dog expert Murat Cengiz Koca said that the trained dogs stayed calm and didn’t react to sounds or people. Difficult words: anxious (worried and nervous), comfort (to improve the mood), pet (to touch an animal because you like it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Some people worry before flying. At Istanbul Airport, they have a great idea. They have dogs there. The dogs help people feel better before flying. There are five dogs. Travelers can touch the dogs and talk to them. The dogs undergo special training . They learn to stay calm and not react to noises or people. Travelers are very happy. They like the dogs very much. The airport is thinking of having five more dogs in the future. Difficult words: undergo (to take part in something), training (when you are learning something new), calm (not nervous or angry). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The question of why humans have hair on their heads beyond aesthetic concerns has intrigued many. While we’ve evolved to lose body fur, our hairy scalps serve a practical purpose. Christian Skorik, a lab scientist and biologist, explains that hair protects the brain, acting as insulation in cold and preventing overheating in heat. It also absorbs sweat, shields from UV rays, and functions as sensory whiskers. Hair might have played a role in sexual selection historically, but in modern life, alternatives like hats provide similar benefits. Thus, while hair isn’t vital , it serves various important functions. Difficult words: aesthetic (concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty), intrigue (to puzzle), vital (necessary). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Many people wonder why humans have hair on their heads. While our ancestors, people who lived before us, lost body fur , and hair on the head seems to be really practical. It keeps the brain safe because it is insulation in cold, on the other hand, it stops the brain from overheating when it is too hot. Also, hair absorbs sweat and protects the skin from UV rays. Scientists believe that in the past, hair played an important role in choosing a sexual partner. But these days, hats protect our heads, so hair doesn’t seem as important anymore. Difficult words: fur (the short soft hair of some animals), insulation (material which protects something or someone from heat or cold), sweat (a salty liquid which we have on our skin when we are hot). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many people wonder why we have hair on our heads. Do we need hair? We have hair for important reasons. Hair keeps our brain safe. It keeps us warm in cold weather. It also helps to cool us down when it is too hot outside. Hair keeps UV rays away from our skin. UV rays are not healthy for our skin. Hair can be like whiskers to warn us of something dangerous. In the past, hair probably helps people choose the right partner. These days it is not so important. But we have hats. They can do the same job as hair. Difficult words: brain (the organ in our head which controls all body), ray (a narrow line in which light streams), whisker (a long hair which grows from the face of many animals). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The fungal kingdom is a vast and wild world. Scientists estimate that up to 12 million species remain undiscovered. Often called dark fungi, these microscopic or hidden organisms elude discovery but are all around us. Although historically misclassified as plants due to their root-like networks, fungi are biologically closer to animals. Over a billion years, they evolved diverse ecological roles. Many form essential partnerships with plants as they exchange soil nutrients for carbon, a relationship that originally helped plants colonize land 470 million years ago. Other fungi produce complex chemical weapons like antibiotics or psilocybin to deter predators, while some, like Cordyceps, turn ants into zombies to spread their spores. Remarkably, certain species thrive in extreme environments like Chernobyl. They use melanin to absorb harmful radiation and convert it into energy. Globally, vast underground fungal networks store massive amounts of carbon, which helps keep the planet resilient against climate change. Difficult words: fungal (relating to or caused by fungi), vast (extremely big, huge, or wide in size, area, or amount), elude (to escape from someone or something, or to avoid being found, caught, or understood), psilocybin (a natural chemical compound found in certain mushrooms that changes how the brain works and causes people to see things that are not real). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The world of fungi is huge and surprising, and scientists think there are millions of undiscovered species. For a long time, people thought fungi were plants because they grow in the soil. But they are closer to animals, and their cell walls are made of chitin, just like insects. Fungi play many important roles in nature. Many plants cannot live without fungi, which give them nutrients from the ground. Some fungi use strong chemicals to protect themselves, like mushrooms with hallucinogenic molecules. Others are dangerous, like the zombie fungus, which controls the bodies of ants. Amazingly, some fungi can even live in radioactive places like Chernobyl and use radiation as a source of energy. These underground fungal networks are very important for the Earth because they store carbon and protect our climate. Difficult words: huge (very big), nutrient (a substance or chemical that plants, animals, and people need to live, grow, and stay healthy), hallucinogenic (causing a person to see, hear, or feel things that do not exist in reality). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Fungi are a very large and special group of living things. This group includes mushrooms, yeast, and millions of other species . Fungi look like plants, but they are closer to animals. They do not get energy from the Sun; they eat other materials. Fungi are very important to nature. They help plants grow. They give them food from the soil . Some fungi do strange things, like changing ants into zombies or smelling like bad meat. This way, they attract flies. Other strong fungi can live in dangerous radioactive places like Chernobyl. Big fungal networks keep carbon underground. This keeps the planet safe from climate change. Difficult words: species (a specific group of living things), soil (the brown substance on the ground where plants and trees grow), attract (to make someone interested in coming to a place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Five days after two catastrophic earthquakes struck Venezuela’s northern coast near Caracas, rescue teams are desperately searching the rubble for survivors. While more than 1,700 people are confirmed dead, the final death toll is expected to rise significantly because approximately 46,000 people remain unaccounted for. In coastal towns like Caraballeda, volunteers use specialized radar equipment and their bare hands to locate signs of life beneath collapsed buildings. Despite fading hopes, miraculous rescues keep families motivated. A mother and her baby were recently saved after being trapped for days; she kept her son alive by checking his breathing whenever he cried. However, at many disaster sites, official counting has paused. Critics openly accuse the Venezuelan government of intentionally delaying the publication of accurate casualty numbers and point out a long history of systematically hiding bad news from the public. At the same time, thousands of families continue to wait in fear of bad news. Difficult words: death toll (the total number of people who die because of a specific bad event, such as an accident, war, or disaster), unaccounted (missing), casualty (a person who is injured or killed in a serious accident, war, or natural disaster). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Two big earthquakes recently hit the coast of Venezuela near the capital city. Five days after the disaster, rescue workers and volunteers are still looking for people under collapsed buildings. More than 1,700 people are dead, but the real number will be much higher because 46,000 people are still missing. In some towns, workers use special radar tools to hear people talking under the rocks. Families still have hope because of beautiful stories, like a mother and her small baby who were saved alive after days in the dark. The searching is very difficult and slow. Many people say that the government is not telling the truth about the total number of dead people because they want to hide the bad news from the world. Difficult words: volunteer (a person who offers to do a job or help other people without being paid for it), radar (a special electronic machine which uses radio waves to find objects or people), hide (to put something in a place where nobody can see it or find it, or to keep information secret). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Two big earthquakes hit Venezuela. The houses on the coast are broken. More than 1,700 people are dead, and 46,000 people are still missing . Families are very sad, but they are still looking for their loved ones. Some workers use their hands and special machines to find people under the rocks. But there are happy stories, too. A mother and her baby come out alive after five days. The mother helps her baby stay strong. People are angry at the leaders. They think that the leaders are lying about the bad news and the true number of dead people. Difficult words: missing (when nobody knows where you are), alive (living and not dead), true (right, correct). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
